PropCast · design refinement spec · v2 · for Junaid

Make it crisp: the five fixes

The concept and the journey are locked. This spec covers the remaining visual layer: why reference sites feel clear and ours feels busy, the exact overlay recipe, the engine's identity problem, the beam spec, the map's loudness budget, and a font system for the whole product. Everything here is implementable with values, not vibes.

01The one principle — SHOW or SAY, never both at full volume

Watch motionsites.ai/?prompt=urban-jungle-hero. When the visual is the hero, there is almost no text. When the text arrives, the visual physically steps back: darker, softer, quieter — and the type lands huge on the calm. It works exactly like audio in a video edit: you duck the music under the voiceover. Our site currently plays music and voiceover at full volume simultaneously, so both lose. Same pixels below — the only difference is the duck:

It already knows what your market is searching for.

NOW — TEXT FIGHTS THE SCENE

Full-brightness map, full-intensity heat, live beams, AND the headline — all at once. The eye has four heroes, so it has none.

It already knows what your market is searching for.

Every ZIP. Every question. Ranked by intent.
TARGET — SCENE DUCKS UNDER THE TEXT

The exact recipe: during any text beat, dim the 3D to ~38% brightness, desaturate ~40%, blur 1.5px, add a radial scrim (rgba(3,6,10,0.72) behind the text column), raise type one size. Camera holds still. When the text exits, the scene comes back up. 15 lines of code, night and day.

Scroll rule: every beat is either a SHOW beat (camera moves, scene at 100%, max one small kicker) or a SAY beat (camera holds, scene ducks, one sentence lands big). Alternate. Never both.

02The type system — pick one, see it live

These are rendered in the actual fonts (all free on Google Fonts, usable today for web + product + docs). The system needs three roles: a Display voice (headlines), a UI voice (product, body), and a Data voice (mono chips, tickers, coordinates). Never more than these three families anywhere in PropertyIQ.

03The engine — it reads as a microscope; make it a held mind

Diagnosis of why it reads wrong today: (1) the form is a tube aimed down at the map — tube + lens + pointed at specimen = microscope, instantly; (2) the housing is ~70% of the object and the graph only ~30%, so the eye reads “instrument,” not “mind”; (3) the graph inside is an unstructured scribble at that scale — uniform dots, no hierarchy. The fix is not more detail. It's a different ratio and a different grip:

  • Flip the ratio: graph 70%, machine 30%. The knowledge graph becomes a large luminous sphere; the machine shrinks to a thin split-ring gimbal (two or three machined arcs) that cradles it at the poles. Held, not contained. No tube, no barrel, nothing aimed at anything.
  • Give the graph anatomy. 60–80 nodes max at hero distance: 5–7 hub nodes at 3–4x size, mid connectors, faint leaves. Edges brighten near hubs. Slow 8-second rotation. A structured constellation reads as a mind; uniform confetti reads as static.
  • Make ingestion visible. The ribbons from the map dock at outer nodes; each docking node flashes amber and cools to cyan as it joins the graph. Cause and effect is what makes it look intelligent.
  • One resolve moment per loop. Every ~8 seconds the graph converges a pulse to its brightest hub and emits one clean return beam to one house on the map. Input, thought, answer — legible from across the room.
Target feel: the graph is the object. Housing reduced to a thin ring. This is the reference we chose — the machine IS a knowledge graph, gripped by minimal hardware.
Alternative skin, same rules: a crisper geometric lattice version. Either skin works — what matters is R1 to R4: ratio, anatomy, ingestion, resolve.

04The beams — from spider web to six labeled rivers

The build spec: each ribbon is a tapered mesh (wide at the street, narrow at the engine) with a bright emissive core and soft dark edge, 3 to 5 particles flowing up it per second, and its source label pinned at the origin. Six to eight ribbons maximum. Delete the rest. Labels are what turn decoration into meaning: the machine stops drinking anonymous spaghetti and starts visibly consuming LOCAL SEARCHES and MLS DATA.

05The map — right detail, wrong loudness (and the city doesn't matter)

The map got dramatically better and the heat legend is a win. The remaining problem isn't complexity — it's that every layer is loud at once: white roads, teal water, green parks, orange heat, glowing pins. A map is the stage, not the show. Give it a brightness budget:

LayerBudgetNote
Buildings10–15% greytexture, never white; kill rooftop highlights
Roads~30% warm greycurrently near-white — the single loudest offender
Water / parks15–20%, desaturatedteal pools currently compete with the heat ramp's own green
Heat layerup to 100%~65% opacity so streets read through; soft falloff; one white-hot core
Pins + ribbons100%the only things allowed to glow

Which city? It genuinely doesn't matter — pick for readability, not geography. Two requirements: (1) residential fabric, not a skyscraper downtown (a low-rise grid of little rooftops says “your farm” to every agent and has far less geometric noise), and (2) one natural edge for composition — a coastline, river, or bay so the grid doesn't run to infinity. Any clean American suburb extract satisfies this. Keep one city consistent across every card, ZIP, and address in the journey, whichever one it is.

06The messaging — one sentence, landing hard

The copy beats are conceptually right. The delivery rules that make them pop like Urban Jungle:

  • One sentence per beat. If a beat needs two sentences, it's two beats. Side labels appear one at a time, never four on screen together.
  • Eight words or fewer for headlines. Current lines mostly pass: “It doesn't guess what to post. It knows.” is the model — keep that register everywhere.
  • Type enters after the camera settles — fade + 16px rise, 250ms, then holds on the ducked scene. Never animates while the camera flies.
  • One accent word per headline in cyan (or the serif italic if System E). Everything else stays white.
  • Kill the ghost text. The faded pre-state of upcoming headlines is currently visible behind the active one — pre-state opacity should be 0, not 15%.
  • Word choice: revert “Guess which one is fake” to “One of these was filmed. Guess which.” Never put the word “fake” next to our own content.

07Priority order for the next sprint

  • The duck (Section 01) — cheapest fix, biggest perceived-quality jump on every beat at once
  • Beams → six labeled ribbons (Section 04)
  • Engine ratio flip + graph anatomy (Section 03)
  • Map brightness budget + one consistent city (Section 05)
  • Type system adoption (Section 02) + messaging rules (Section 06)
